info.title: Nex Core pool peer API
info.description: Internal Core-to-Core pool peer contract; not a client or Controller API. Nex Controller never calls it and holds none of its state: membership, the pool CA, repository reservations, pool VM execution records and clustered-storage operations are durable on the pool master Core (peer probe leases and access observations are process-local). Served on the dedicated peer HTTPS listener (--pool-peer-listen, default :9444, on nex-core-local and nex-core-agent), TLS 1.3 only, with server limits of 5 s header, 15 s read, 30 s write and 16 KiB headers. The listener requests a client certificate and verifies it against the pool CA when presented; every route except join then admits only the peer named by its security requirement. Clients pin the pool CA and expected host ID (and, master to member, the membership certificate SHA-256), refuse redirects and time out after 15 s. Errors are short text/plain bodies. Development protocol: deploy matching Core versions in a pool; additive acknowledgements (probe mode echo, update_accepted, spec_match) let newer peers fail closed against older ones. Controller-hosted qnetd witness candidate and certificate-registration routes are implemented for Core; two-host SBD arming and witness-loss promotion proof remain withheld.

post.summary: Advertise member peer origin and host observations
post.description: Served by the pool master over authenticated member mTLS. Records only the calling member own peer listener origin, system UUID, management-controller and watchdog observations in Core membership. The certificate selects the member; body input cannot name another. Repeats with unchanged values do not rewrite authority. A pending origin is retried by Core. Body at most 4 KiB.

get.summary: Probe what pool authority this host holds
get.description: Read-only. Admitted to any holder of a certificate this pool's CA issued, including one this pool has ejected: an ejected host must be able to learn that it is no longer a member, and it can only learn that from the pool that ejected it. The caller's own membership status is decided from the certificate the transport proved, never from a name in a body. A pool master answering a ready member that is behind also returns a pool-CA-signed re-point notice, so a host that missed a push converges from whichever host it can reach without having to trust a stale one; the probe answer alone changes nothing, only the signature at a strictly higher generation does. Optional query ?vms=1 adds this host's own view of the VM definitions it owns, which the promotion proof of a later slice consumes. The handler also accepts POST with an identical, equally read-only answer, so a caller behind a transport that dislikes one method can use the other; nothing in Nex Core calls the POST form, so it is described here rather than documented as a separate operation.

post.summary: Submit backup or test cleanup work to a member
post.description: The current pool master sends backup-now or test-cleanup with its Core-owned NFS repository source and observed filesystem identity. Restore commands use the catalog-bound /api/v1/pool/backup/restore route. A repeated operation ID returns the retained result only for the same command; changed input is refused. post.summary: Report what this host found on the other hosts' fence devices
post.description: Served by the pool master. Every ready host periodically reads every other host's management controller over the recorded fence profile and the replicated credential, asking which machine it manages and reading that machine's power state, and sends the results here. The read is non-destructive by construction: no power-off is reachable from that code path. The member certificate says which host is calling and the whole report is credited to that host; a claim it makes about its own row is dropped, because a host does not get to say whether it can be shut out. The master keeps these in memory, overlays them on the membership it reports and never writes them into its durable membership record, so a pool's signed authority does not move because a check ran; a master that restarts reports "not checked yet" until the next pass. Safe to repeat: a later report replaces the caller's previous one. Body at most 64 KiB.

post.summary: Offer the pool master the fence device this host configured on its own controller
post.description: Served by the pool master. The member certificate says which host is calling and the profile is recorded for that host only: a member cannot offer a fence device for another host. The master writes the password into its own private fence-credential store first, because the identity check that follows signs in with it, and then records the profile through exactly the path an operator-entered profile takes — including proving over the network that the controller really manages that host's machine, and refusing to replace a profile an operator entered by hand. Nothing is recorded if any step refuses, and the refusal sentence is returned so the member can report it. Idempotent in effect: a member that has already had its profile recorded does not call this again, and a repeat records the same profile with fresh material. Body at most 8 KiB.

post.summary: Redeem a pool join offer
post.description: Served by the pool master; the only peer route without a client certificate. Authority is the single-use offer created by the master Core local API: it binds pool, master host, member host ID and CSR SHA-256, and expires after 15 minutes. The master signs the CSR with the pool CA, appends the member as ready, increments the membership generation and persists before replying. A retry of the same offer, host ID and CSR after a lost response returns the same certificate and current membership; a different key or an already-admitted host is refused. The member pins the pool CA and master host ID from the offer, verifies the returned certificate against its pending key, then persists and completes a Core-owned rehome. Body at most 1 MiB.

post.summary: Check one member's native VM placement
post.description: Served by the current ready selected member at its advertised origin and called only by its current pool master over pinned mutual TLS. The request names one exact vm-create or vm-update command and the current membership generation. The member reads its current durable managed state, including the no-effect clustered-storage admission context, and performs no mutation, reservation, or start. It returns only after native placement checks complete and after rechecking membership. The master accepts an acknowledgement only when generation, operation_id, vm_id and vm echo exactly and accepted is true; before saving its definition or reservation it takes its durable locks and rechecks that same membership generation. A missing acknowledgement field from an older Core, timeout, connection failure, refusal or membership change fails placement closed. replay:true means the target recognized the identical existing journal command and did no fresh native check; it may confirm only an existing durable master placement record, never create one. A failed placement admission for an exact journalled definition command does not authorize native execution or journal reconciliation; Core reports needs_attention. Retry only the same operation and command after reconciliation; changed input with the same operation is refused. Requests and master-accepted replies are bounded to 128 KiB; the member's preflight deadline is 20 seconds.

get.summary: Report what authority replica this member holds
get.description: Served by a pool member at its advertised peer origin and called only by its current pool master over pinned mutual TLS. Read-only. It is also how the master learns the member's certified peer public key for the per-member key wrap, from the pinned TLS leaf of this call, so no public key is ever put on the wire or into the membership record. An empty object is returned when this host holds no replica. Answering also refreshes the member's own observation window, so a member the master is polling does not report its replica as stale.

post.summary: Store one signed authority replica on this member
post.description: Master to member over pinned mutual TLS, bounded to 1 MiB with no trailing JSON. The member verifies that the replica names its own pool and its current master, is addressed to itself, declares every section with matching digests, and is signed by the pool CA it pinned at join; it then writes pool-replica.json atomically at mode 0600 and acknowledges. It never acts on the contents: no membership, VM, storage, network or media record on this host is read from or changed by a replica, a replica grants no execution, and no health judgement is derived from one. Idempotent: the same generation with the same content returns the same acknowledgement. A strictly lower generation is refused, and the same generation with different content is refused rather than overwriting. The wrapped pool CA key is stored sealed and is not opened by anything in this release. Pushes are driven by the master's probe tick when its authority content digest has changed or a member is behind, so a member may lag by up to one probe interval; nothing waits on a replica.

409.description: Refused and not stored; whatever this host already held is unchanged. The bounded reason is one of "pool authority replica names another pool", "pool authority replica is not from the current pool master", "pool authority replica is addressed to another host", "pool authority replica is not signed by this pool's CA", "pool authority replica does not declare every section", "pool authority replica section digest does not match", "pool authority replica generation is older than the stored replica", "pool authority replica generation was already stored with different contents", "pool authority replica VM ownership record is invalid", "pool authority replica omitted the qdevice credential addressed to this member", "pool authority replica omitted the Corosync key", "pool authority replica could not be stored", "pool membership is unavailable", "pool peer state is unavailable", "stored pool authority replica is unavailable", or a PoolAuthorityReplica.Valid() text. Refusal also includes "pool authority replica backup pages are incomplete or invalid" when a signed backup manifest names missing or corrupt staged pages.

post.summary: Stage one signed backup authority page in a push session
post.description: The current pool master sends content-addressed backup authority pages over pinned mutual TLS in a signed, addressed push session. A signed replica with index -1 and null data opens a session (10-minute expiry, one per member) and returns the next missing page. Page requests name manifest_sha256 and index with page bytes or reuse_sha256; another manifest or master is refused with 409. Each page and complete frame is at most 256 KiB. Cleanup kind-7 frames contain {cleanup,point_count}, where cleanup.points is null; exactly point_count contiguous kind-8 BackupOrphanPointResult frames follow, across pages if necessary. Counts, unique cleanup identities, frame validity, total bytes and the ordered full-stream SHA-256 root are verified before final adoption. No history is truncated. Reuse links an already durable page blob, or returns 404 for bytes to be resent. Opening a complete session verifies the full root; content mismatch clears staging, while read failure returns 500 without clearing it. Collection preserves acknowledged and unexpired-upload roots. Staged pages grant no authority. Matching updated Core peers must be deployed and authority repushed from the durable current master before promotion; old cleanup framing fails closed in either direction.
post.x-audience: Core peer: pool master → pool member

post.summary: Hold a cross-Core probe lock lease
post.description: Served by the pool master. Takes a non-blocking OFD write lock on one byte of .nex-peer-lock in the repository path so the member can prove it observes the same shared filesystem (it must see a conflict, then acquire after DELETE). challenge-byte-v1 uses a nonzero offset derived from SHA-256 of the challenge and echoes X-Nex-Pool-Probe-Mode; absent probe_mode uses legacy byte zero. The lease is bound to caller, repository, generation, challenge and mode; replaying the same held lease returns 204. Leases expire after ten seconds, at most 64 are active, and they are not VM ownership or fencing authority.

post.summary: Admit a pool VM execution transition
post.description: Served by the pool master, serialized per master. The owner member asks the master to durably record a VM definition or execution transition before acting locally; the master writes its record before replying. For define(create=true) and update-reserve, before taking the durable VM lock the master obtains the selected current member's exact authenticated native placement preflight; no lock spans that RPC. It validates returned shared-storage observations and persists the definition or exact next revision before setting placement_accepted=true. Actions: define (create=true seeds a new record from a valid vm owned by the caller; otherwise spec_match reports whether vm matches the durable definition and refuses a pending snapshot recovery reservation), start (defined/stopped → starting, epoch+1, returns a random permit), running (starting → running), stop (owner check only), stopped (owner proves stop; placement retained), reboot (requires running) and media (owner check only), update-reserve (reserve one exact next revision), update-commit and update-abort (settle it with exact local journal evidence). Only the recorded owner may transition a VM; there is no expiry or timeout cleanup, so unknown execution stays fenced and an unreachable host is never treated as stopped. Retries after a lost reply reconcile the exact durable definition or reservation; a missing placement_accepted acknowledgement, preflight timeout or membership change fails closed. Body at most 1 MiB. The snapshot-reserve action binds the exact snapshot request, native intent digest and timestamp to the owner epoch/spec, refuses running VMs and pending storage mutations, and persists a bounded catalog reservation under the same authority lock. Snapshot-create reservations also bind a nonzero monotonic owner_operation_order. The snapshot-metadata action updates only a settled catalog name and description for an existing snapshot ID owned by the caller; digests and creation time stay fixed. Duplicate-name and full-catalog denials are persisted as exact admission_refusal values and require matching failed-before-effects settlement; a delayed operation order at or below the same owner's settled watermark is rejected, including after ordinary owner epoch changes. The release-restore-placement action is sent only by the executing current member after it has observed no native journal, domain, target disk directory, NVRAM or TPM state for a failed restore-as-new/test operation. The master requires placement_absent=true, caller matching vm.host_id, the exact pending backup run and creator operation in its durable VM owner row, full VM spec, an untouched defined epoch-1 owner and no observed inventory VM. It durably deletes only that provisional row, then echoes placement_released=true; an exact repeat after a lost reply also acknowledges. Missing creator provenance, changed ownership, uncertain absence or an unreachable master leave the restore at needs_attention.

A bridge or libvirt network already held by another registration on that host is a failed host result, not an HTTP 409.

origin.description: Bare https:// origin: no user info, path, query or fragment. It may be omitted or empty when system_uuid is sent on its own.

system_uuid.description: This member's own SMBIOS system UUID, in any usual spelling; the master normalizes it to 32 lower-case hex digits and refuses known firmware placeholders (all-zero, all-ff and the common 03000200-0400-0500-0006-000700080009). Recorded in the member's membership row and used to prove a management controller belongs to this machine before a fence powers it off. The master records it only in the calling member's own row, and refuses two changes that would let a host defeat its own fencing: replacing an identity it already reported while a BMC fence profile is recorded against it (clearing the profile is the motherboard-replacement path), and claiming an identity another member of the pool already holds. A refused value is dropped silently — the request still returns 204 when the origin was recorded — and the member simply cannot be given a BMC fence device. Members send it at join and on every reconcile pass, so a pool formed before this existed gains it without re-joining; a member too old to send one is unaffected.

bmc.description: What this member's own Nex Core found and did about its own management controller. Recorded in the calling member's own row; the state must be one of the closed set and the sentence is bounded at 1 KiB, or the request is refused with 400. It is an observation and nothing more: a host cannot change what the pool decided about it, so a report of state "removed" does not delete the fence device the pool recorded — withdrawing one is an operator decision authenticated at the Controller and recorded by the master. A report that does not differ from the one already recorded, except in its timestamp, is not written at all, so a settled pool's signed authority does not move because a host keeps saying the same thing. Like the other two fields it may be sent on its own and it moves no membership generation.

watchdog.description: The watchdog device this member's own Nex Core found on the machine it runs on, read from sysfs without ever opening the device node. Recorded in the calling member's own row; the kind must be one of the closed set and the strings are bounded, or the request is refused with 400. Like the other fields it is an observation, it may be sent on its own, it moves no membership generation, and a report that does not differ from the one already recorded is not written at all, so a settled pool's signed authority does not move because a host keeps saying the same thing. Members send it on every reconcile pass, so a pool formed before this existed gains it without re-joining; a member too old to send one leaves the field absent, which never counts as a watchdog.

watchdog_armed.description: This member's own report that it has armed the watchdog above, recorded in the calling member's own row. It is the first of the three conditions of a watchdog exclusion proof, so unlike the capability beside it the master keeps it durably and replicates it: the host that has to read it is a promotion candidate whose master has gone. Refused with 400 if the kind is not one a watchdog exclusion could rest on, or the strings are unbounded. A report that does not differ from the one already recorded is not written at all, so a settled pool's signed authority does not move because a reconcile pass ran. A member too old to send one leaves the field absent, which never counts.

sanlock_host_generation.description: This member's own observed generation in its configured sanlock lockspace. The master records it in the member row for future proof checks; it is not proof by itself.

PeerAdvertiseRequest.description: What a member advertises about itself through authenticated peer mTLS: origin, machine identity, management controller, watchdog and observed sanlock generation. Each field is recorded on its own when safe.

PeerJoinRequest.description: Untagged Go struct: JSON members use Go field names (case-insensitive on decode). Offer is the raw offer token, not the encoded offer.

CSRPEM.description: PEM certificate request whose subject CN equals HostID and whose SHA-256 matches the offer.

hostname.description: Name reported by the joining Core for its durable membership row: required, at most 200 UTF-8 bytes of printable characters with no leading or trailing space. The Go encoding omits an empty value, so the schema does not list it under required, but the master refuses a join without one (409); a joiner that predates hostname reporting must be upgraded and restarted.

PeerJoinResponse.description: Signed member certificate (TLS client and server auth, two-year validity) and the master membership after admission.

from_host_id.description: The host that issued and signed this notice.

target_host_id.description: The transfer's subject: the promoted host, or the ejected one.

authority_generation.description: The exact authority generation being handed over, or the generation the issuing master holds.

signature.description: Base64 ASN.1 ECDSA P-256/SHA-256 over the whole notice minus this field, made with the pool CA key. Every recipient verifies it against the pool CA it pinned at join, so no host takes another host's word for who the master is.

PoolAuthorityNotice.description: The pool-CA-signed statement that pool authority moved. Used twice in one transfer: the hand-off, signed by the outgoing master, naming the exact generation it froze and the host it handed that generation to (membership empty); and the re-point, signed by the new master with the pool CA key it now holds, carrying the new membership at a strictly higher membership generation. A notice without a signature, or at a generation that is not strictly higher, is refused.

generation.description: The pool master's own durable authority generation. This is the only absolute generation in the pool; nothing else derives one.

digest.description: SHA-256 of the authority content that generation numbered.

PoolAuthorityRecord.description: Reported by the pool master alone. A Controller mirrors it to compare each member's acknowledged replica generation against it and stores neither.

PoolAuthorityReplica.description: The pool master's signed, read-only copy of its own durable pool authority, pushed to one member. It is stored by every ready member and acted on by none of them: no membership, VM, storage, network, media or in-progress resource mutation on the receiving host is read from or changed by a replica, and no health judgement is derived from one. The signature is made with the pool CA key over every field but signature, so a member verifies it against the pool CA it pinned at join, long after the master that signed it is gone. Bounded to 1 MiB on the wire and on disk.

generation.description: The master's authority generation, which it advances only when the replicated content digest changes. Never 0 in a valid replica; generations may skip.

member_host_id.description: The one member this copy is addressed to. It is inside the signature, so a replica cannot be re-addressed in transit and a copy wrapped for one member cannot be presented to another.

vms.description: The master's pool-vms.json owner projection, replicated as received bytes so ownership, epochs, specs and pending updates survive unchanged. Published per-host inventory snapshots are deliberately not replicated: they are observations, and a promoted master re-collects fresh ones.

storage.description: Pool storage registrations with credential receipts stripped, exactly as the storage peer list strips them.

fence_credentials.description: The pool's fence credential material, sealed for this member alone. Like ca_key_wrapped it is covered by signature and excluded from the content digest, so one generation still has one digest for every member; what makes new material advance the generation is fence_credential_version in the membership.

sections.description: Exactly the seven sections above, in order.

signature.description: Base64 ASN.1 ECDSA P-256/SHA-256 signature by the pool CA key over the whole replica with signature empty.

witness_credentials.description: Per-member sealed native qdevice credentials. The shared qdevice key is wrapped separately to each member and bound to the fencing generation.

resource_mutations.description: In-progress destructive network or media removals, replicated so promotion cannot forget an unresolved outcome.

backup_manifest.description: Paged backup authority reference; the pages are pushed separately and bound by the manifest root.

corosync_key_wrapped.description: Pool Corosync authentication key sealed for this member and replica generation; required when the pool forms its own cluster.

update_rollout.description: The master's pool-update.json, declared as the section update_rollout only while a record exists (a pool that never rolled out keeps the older section layout). A promoted master adopts an active rollout paused master_changed.

host_id.description: The host that answered the probe.

role.description: This host's own role in the pool it names.

master_host_id.description: The host this host currently follows as pool master.

master_peer_origin.description: That master's peer origin, so a converging host can go on to probe it.

authority_generation.description: This host's own pool authority generation; 0 on a member.

membership_generation.description: The membership generation this host holds.

replica_generation.description: The generation of the authority replica this host stores.

replica_verified.description: Whether that replica was proven against the pool CA.

frozen.description: This host is refusing pool authority writes for a transfer.

handed_off.description: This host has signed its authority away and refuses every authority write for good, not only while frozen.

caller_status.description: The membership status this host holds for the calling certificate, decided from the certificate the transport proved rather than from a name in a body. Empty when it names no member at all. This is how an ejected host learns it has been ejected.

transfer.description: This host's own part of a transfer.

notice.description: A master answers a ready member that is behind with a signed re-point notice, so a host that missed a push converges from whichever host it can reach without having to trust a stale one. The probe answer alone changes nothing; only the signature at a strictly higher generation does.

restricted.description: This host's own refusal to act on pool authority, set while it cannot prove it holds the pool's current authority. A returning fenced master answers its probes with this, which is how a member and an operator see that it came back and is refusing to start anything.

vms.description: This host's own view of the VM definitions it owns, answered only when the caller asks with ?vms=1. Consumed by the promotion proof of a later slice.

vms_reported.description: Separates "this host defines no VM" from "this host could not read its own record": an empty vms list means the first only when this is true.

PoolAuthorityStatus.description: The read-only authority probe every host answers to any holder of a certificate this pool's CA issued, including one this pool has ejected. It is how a returning or restarted host discovers that it has been superseded or ejected, and how a host that missed a re-point finds the current master without trusting a stale one.

PoolBackupAuthority.description: Bounded replica section for backup repositories, policy/schedule definitions, retained runs and catalog index. Full NFS recovery-point payloads are never embedded.

repositories.description: Durable backup destination registrations (NFS, SMB3, S3 and SFTP) for master takeover.

definitions.description: Full committed policy/schedule definitions for master takeover.

history.description: Retained and unresolved backup/restore run records for master takeover.

catalog.description: Master catalog index entries only; NFS payloads are never embedded.

policies.description: Compact policy refs derived from definitions for observation.

runs.description: Compact run refs derived from history for observation.

pins.description: Active per-operation restore pins transferred to the new master before retention can prune. Several pins may refer to the same recovery point; operation IDs are unique.

metadata_receipts.description: Durable operation result receipts retained for exact metadata retry after master takeover.

orphan_cleanups.description: Orphaned-backup cleanup records retained so the new master still answers for a cleanup the old master ran.

PoolBackupManifest.description: Signed backup authority reference. It binds ordered page_count, total_bytes, full SHA-256 root and record counts; every page is at most 256 KiB. The member verifies the full root, frames, unique IDs and counts before acknowledging.

replica.description: Signed replica; present only on the request that opens a push session (index -1).

index.description: Zero-based page index; -1 with the signed replica and empty data opens a push session and returns next-page progress.

data.description: Base64 page bytes; null with a version-2 reuse_sha256 hint or an index -1 progress probe.

reuse_sha256.description: Digest of an already durable 256 KiB-or-smaller page blob. Data must be null; missing/corrupt blob returns 404 so the master sends bytes instead.

manifest_sha256.description: Root of the manifest verified when the session opened; required on page requests.

operation_id.description: Stable operation ID issued by the master.

command.description: Master-issued backup or restore command. The payload matching kind and the owner host identity are required; other command payloads are omitted.

catalog_point.description: Required on the restore-only peer route; omitted for backup-now and cleanup.

smb_identity.description: Master-observed SMB3 share marker; required for SMB3 backup/restore work and verified by the member before effects. Omitted for NFS and test cleanup.

intent_sha256.description: Member durable command-intent digest; master compares it to its reserved run before settlement.

run.description: Member durable run stage/evidence when available.

catalog_manifest_sha256.description: Durable member restore-run catalog manifest digest. Required in a restore reply; master compares it with its pinned catalog point before settlement.

features.description: Optional fixed native CPU feature list. Omitted or empty retains model-only behavior. Nonempty requires a named model (not host modes or max) and vm-cpu-baseline-v1. Duplicate feature names are rejected.

cpu.description: Native guest CPU XML derived from libvirt host-model capabilities, including feature overrides.

membership.description: The full membership record for the pool actions that carry one. For join and maintenance only master_host_id is set: the master reads its own record, and a membership composed in the Controller could already be stale.

expected_version.description: The membership generation the operator saw. 0 or absent means unchecked. For action maintenance it is compared against the master's own current membership generation, not against the membership on the wire.

member_host_id.description: For action join, the joining host: it is the command's target, and the pool-join command is the one pool command not delivered to the master. For action maintenance it names the host being drained, which is not the target: that command goes to the master, addressed by membership.master_host_id.

enabled.description: For action maintenance, the desired drain state of member_host_id. It is a desired state, not a transition: re-sending the state the host is already in succeeds and leaves maintenance_since unmoved.

master_url.description: Bare HTTPS origin of the master's pool-peer listener that the joining Core dials. Required for action join.

pool_ca_pem.description: Master's pool CA, pinned by the joining Core for the peer exchange. Required for action join. Never returned by any Controller read route.

invitation.description: Single-use, 15-minute, pool- and host-bound join credential issued by the master and redeemed by the joining Core itself. Required for action join. The Controller relays it and never returns, lists, logs or audits it; the stored command row is scrubbed of this field and pool_ca_pem as soon as the operation leaves queued, and unconditionally 15 minutes after issue.

peer_origin.description: Optional bare HTTPS origin the joining host advertises to its new master after it is admitted.

fence.description: The power-fence profile to record for member_host_id, on action fence-profile. null clears the recorded profile. Any credential the operator supplied has already been delivered to Core over the one-time encrypted credential handoff before this command is written, and only the opaque reference Core allocated appears here.

fence_confirmed.description: The operator's separate, explicit acknowledgement that promoting this candidate powers the old pool master off. It is a precondition and nothing else: Core produces and verifies the fence proof itself, no proof ever crosses this wire, and an acknowledgement is never evidence of anything.

fence_host_ids.description: The exact set of hosts the operator agreed to power off, as the verdict's fence_host_ids named them. Core compares it against the set it computes again at run time and refuses the promotion if they differ, so the fence can never widen between the confirmation and the act.

update.description: Request of the update-rollout and update-control actions.

PoolCommand.description: membership is required for the member-join and storage-reconcile actions and is absent for join and maintenance: a joining host is not a member yet, and the master reads its own membership rather than trusting a Controller mirror. Valid() requires request_id plus, for action join, member_host_id, master_url, pool_ca_pem and invitation within the lengths above.

host_id.description: The other host of the pair. A member reports it as the host it checked; the pool master reports it back as the host that did the checking, because the checks are listed on the row of the host they are about.

result.description: ok: the controller answered, accepted the recorded account and named this host's own machine. unreachable: it did not answer, or did not report the machine it manages. credentials_rejected: it refused the recorded account. identity_mismatch: it named a different machine, which is not a network fault and never a pass. certificate_changed: it presented a certificate other than the one the profile is pinned to. tool_missing: this Nex Core has no ipmitool. no_profile: no fence device is recorded for that host. unusable: the profile could never produce a proof, for example a host with no unique hardware identity.

detail.description: Core's own sentence for that result, shown verbatim. Never a credential.

power.description: The machine's power state as the controller reported it; absent when the controller did not say. Reported, never acted on.

profile.description: Binds this result to the fence device it was taken against: 16 hex characters over the profile's kind, address, target, account, pinned certificate and cipher, plus the hardware identity it is compared with. The pool master drops every result whose stamp is not the one its membership records now, so a replaced profile cannot inherit the checks taken against the one before it and reads as not checked yet until the next pass.

observed_at.description: When the pool master last had this result confirmed, on the master's own clock, so freshness never depends on two hosts agreeing about the time. Set by the master; a member does not send it.

stale.description: The master has not had this result confirmed for longer than it vouches for (three check intervals). A stale check is shown as stale and is never readiness.

PoolFenceCheck.description: One host's non-destructive read of another host's fence device: the management controller's own report of which machine it manages, and whether that machine is powered on, over the recorded profile and the replicated credential. Nothing on that path can power anything off. It is a Core observation and never enters the master's durable membership record.

checks.description: At most 64 results, one per host the caller looked at. An entry naming the caller itself is dropped: a host does not get to say whether it can be shut out.

PoolFenceCheckRequest.description: One checking pass, as a member sends it to its pool master.

PoolFenceCluster.description: The master's memory-only pool cluster observation. Pools of three to five ready hosts can form the watchdog cluster when Host fencing is on and no clustered-storage repository is configured. An eligible two-host pool instead can register Controller-hosted qnetd and configure Corosync qdevice; the reported forming/degraded status reflects qdevice state, but no two-host SBD arming or witness-loss exclusion proof is enabled. Durable witness selection and CA pin are in PoolMembership.witness; native readiness is rechecked after restart.

state.description: off is the pool's Host fencing setting. not_available means the pool has no applicable cluster or witness support. For the three-or-more-host watchdog cluster, forming waits for Corosync quorum, arming is the one-host-at-a-time rollout, and degraded means hosts are not all armed. In an eligible two-host pool, forming means qdevice or native quorum is not verified; it can coexist with an operating witness when Corosync is nonquorate. Degraded means the witness and quorum are operating but two-host watchdog arming remains withheld.

detail.description: Core's own sentence for the state. A client shows it as written.

witness.description: The pool master's current native qdevice observation, separate from watchdog arming. Omitted when no witness is selected.

armed.description: How many hosts of this pool's cluster are feeding a watchdog.

total.description: How many hosts are in this pool's cluster. Every ready host that is not in maintenance is in it: a host is never silently left out of the quorum the rest of the pool makes its decisions with.

arming_host_id.description: The host whose turn it is to arm, by host ID. Arming means restarting that host's cluster services, so exactly one host in a pool does it at a time, and whose turn it is is derived from the membership rather than granted. A host that cannot arm holds the turn and the rollout stops there with that host's own reason, which is the safe direction: fewer armed hosts is less protection, never a false proof.

kind.description: The recorded fence profile's kind (ipmilan, redfish or virsh), or watchdog for the host's own self-fencing method. A host's row carries one entry per method.

state.description: ready: another ready host has a fresh successful check against this device. not_ready: Nex Core knows it would not work, and says why. unknown: Nex Core could not observe it, typically because nothing has checked this host yet. no_peer: this pool has no other host to be checked from, which is not a wait — a pool of one host also has nothing to promote over and needs no fence device. not_applicable: this pool cannot use this method at all, as a watchdog cannot be used below three hosts, and that is not something an operator can fix. Readiness is an observation shown to an operator: nothing here decides a promotion, which is decided by the live fence proof alone.

reason.description: Core's own sentence for a method that is not ready, shown verbatim. It names the host that found the problem, for example "this management controller did not answer (from host-b)".

checks.description: Every other ready host's last non-destructive read of this method against this host.

PoolFenceMethod.description: One way a host could be shut out, and whether it would work.

name.description: Which line of the checklist this is: enough hosts for a majority side, a hardware watchdog on every host, a confirmed fence device on every host, and the pool's quorum.

state.description: unknown is Nex Core saying it cannot observe this yet and is never read as met. Quorum is unknown until this pool runs a quorum service.

detail.description: Core's own sentence for this line, shown verbatim, naming the hosts a line is unmet for.

hosts.description: Which hosts the sentence is about, as host IDs. Nex Core ends detail before naming them and puts them here, because only a client knows their display names.

PoolFencePrerequisite.description: One line of the prerequisite checklist Nex Core reports for arming watchdogs.

fence.description: The profile the member wants recorded for itself. It must be kind ipmilan, provisioned_by_core, and name the Nex fence account; anything else is refused.

password.description: The password of the account the member just created on its own controller. At most 64 characters and no NUL, CR or LF. It travels only over this pool mTLS connection, goes straight into the master's private fence-credential store as the profile's password script, and is never logged, reported, audited or part of any inventory.

PoolFenceProvision.description: A member offering the pool master the fence device its own Core configured in-band.

ready.description: At least one method is ready. No readiness at all, and readiness with no ready method, are both never treated as protected.

PoolFenceReadiness.description: The pool master's own per-method answer to whether this host could be shut out right now. It is derived from the membership the master owns and from the continuous non-destructive checks other hosts report, and is a memory-only observation overlaid on the membership copy the master reports, never part of the durable record. A master that has just restarted reports its methods as unknown until the next check pass rather than keeping a durable store of something one interval re-establishes.

ready.description: How many of this pool's ready hosts another host could shut out.

total.description: How many ready hosts this pool has. An ejected host is a tombstone in the membership, not one of this pool's hosts, and a host that has not finished joining is not one either; neither is counted.

unready.description: The ready hosts no other host could shut out, by host ID.

host_fencing.description: The pool's Host fencing setting as the master records it. It is on for a pool that has never been told otherwise. On by itself arms nothing: Nex Core arms a host's watchdog only where every prerequisite below holds.

prerequisites.description: Core's own checklist for arming watchdogs, computed on the master over the membership it owns. A client displays it and decides no line of it.

cluster.description: The master's current cluster or qdevice status. This is a memory-only observation. A two-host qdevice may report forming or degraded while SBD arming and witness-loss proof remain withheld. Absent on older masters, which a client shows as no cluster line rather than as a cluster that is off.

PoolFenceSummary.description: The pool's own fencing answer, reported by the master with its membership: how many of this pool's hosts another host could shut out, which ones it could not, the Host fencing setting and Core's prerequisite checklist. A client displays it; it does not add up the rows it is about to render, which would count ejected tombstones and hosts that are still joining.

state.description: What this host's own Nex Core found on its own management controller. provisioned: Core created its fence account and the master recorded the profile. no_local_interface: no /dev/ipmi0, so there is nothing to configure from the inside. user_management_refused: the controller refused in-band account management, or has no free user slot. lan_disabled: the controller reports no LAN address on any channel, or offers no authenticated RMCP+ cipher suite. name_conflict: an account under the Nex name exists that Core did not create, and nothing was changed. manual_profile: an operator entered a profile, which always wins. removed: an operator removed the account and automatic provisioning stays off for this host. pending_master: the account exists but the master has not recorded the profile yet, so this host has no usable fence device and is never shown as having one.

detail.description: Core's own sentence for that state, shown verbatim. Never a credential.

address.description: The controller's own LAN address as it reports it in-band.

channel.description: The controller's LAN channel the account was created on.

account.description: The account name Core created; not a secret. Its password goes to the master's private fence-credential store and nowhere else.

observed_at.description: When this finding last *changed*, not when it was last confirmed. An unchanged finding is deliberately not re-reported: the membership is signed and replicated, so a moving timestamp would re-sign and re-push the pool's whole authority every reconcile pass. It therefore says nothing about whether the host is still reporting. Liveness is that host's own connection, and the freshness of a fence device is PoolFenceCheck.observed_at, which the pool master stamps on its own clock every time a check is confirmed.

PoolHostBMC.description: One host's own report about its own management controller, kept in the pool master's membership record. It is a Core observation: a fresh Controller recovers it with the rest of the membership and stores nothing of its own. A member too old to report one is absent.

kind.description: Only a device that resets the machine independently of the kernel can count: hardware, and emulated where the host is itself a virtual machine and the hypervisor really does reset it. The kernel's softdog is software — a hung kernel does not run it — so it is reported and reported as not counting. A driver Nex Core does not recognise is unknown and counts as nothing until it is classified.

device.description: The sysfs device name, for example watchdog0. Not a path under /dev: Nex Core never opens the device node, because on most drivers opening it arms the timer.

driver.description: The kernel driver behind the device, which is what the classification is made on.

timeout_seconds.description: The device's configured timeout. Zero means the kernel did not say.

nowayout.description: The kernel's setting that closing the device does not stop the timer. Where it is set, Nex Core cannot disarm this host without rebooting it, and reports that rather than resetting the host to get out of it.

in_use.description: Something already holds the device open, read from sysfs rather than by opening it.

PoolHostWatchdog.description: One host's own report of the watchdog device it has, read from sysfs on the host it is about and recorded by the pool master. A watchdog is how a host shuts itself out, so it has to have been reported while the host was alive. It is a slow-changing capability: it is written only when the finding changes and carries no timestamp, because nothing decides anything from how long ago a host last said it.

hostname.description: Host-reported name retained in the Core master membership and signed replica so a fresh Controller can name an offline member. At most 200 UTF-8 bytes of printable characters.

observed_at.description: When the master admitted this member, or created the pool for its founding host. Nothing rewrites it afterwards; the Controller reports it as joined_at.

peer_origin.description: Bare HTTPS origin this member advertised to the master for peer traffic. Recorded from the member's own advertisement, or, for the master's own row, from the master_url of the first Controller-driven join, which the master works out itself when none is supplied; never inferred from Controller connectivity.

system_uuid.description: This host's own SMBIOS system UUID, 32 lower-case hex digits without separators, reported by the host itself while it was alive: at join, and on every reconcile pass, so a pool formed before this existed gains it without re-joining. It is what proves a management controller belongs to this machine before it is powered off. Like peer_origin it is a recorded observation and moves no generation. A host too old to report one stays empty and simply cannot be given a BMC fence device.

replica_ack_excluded.description: Core-owned exclusion from snapshot reservation/settlement replica acknowledgements and ordinary replica-push failure aggregation, recorded only by a supported promotion after validating fresh exact fence evidence. Omitted means false. The host remains a pool member and VM owner; delivery is still attempted. The master clears the exclusion only after accepted current-membership VM inventory and an exact current-generation/content replica POST acknowledgement. Covered by the signed authority content, without changing membership generation when cleared. It does not exempt destructive resource-removal acknowledgements, storage-lease preparation, restart authority confirmation or future promotion fencing. Use matching development Core builds; old promotions are not retroactively excluded.

replica_generation.description: The master's observation of the authority-replica generation this member last acknowledged. Memory-only on the master and overlaid on the reported copy of the membership record: it is never written into the durable membership and is never an input to the generation equality rule. A member that has never acknowledged one is reported at 0, honestly.

replica_digest.description: Content digest the member acknowledged, as observed by the master.

replica_error.description: The master's bounded reason for the last failed push to this member: "pool member did not report its authority replica", "pool member did not acknowledge the authority replica", "pool member acknowledged the replica without joining the authority sanlock lockspace", "pool member acknowledged the replica without the Corosync key", "pool member refused the authority replica" or the member's own refusal text, "pool authority replica exceeds the peer body limit", or "pool member peer certificate cannot receive a wrapped pool CA key", "pool member did not report backup authority page progress", "pool member reported invalid backup authority page progress", "pool member refused backup authority page reuse", "pool member refused a backup authority page", or a refusal to report/stage a signed backup authority page.

replica_observed_at.description: When the master made that observation. Zero when it has none.

fence.description: How this host would be excluded from the pool if it had to be fenced: the same closed typed profile clustered storage already uses, recorded in the master's durable membership and replicated with it, so a promoted master inherits it and a fresh Controller re-adopts it. Only a virsh profile can be recorded by this build; Core refuses to record a profile it cannot verify. The credential reference it carries is never projected to a client, and neither is anything the reference names.

fence_credential_version.description: The master's counter for the private fence credential material behind this host's profile. The material itself is never in the membership; only this number is, so rotating it changes the replicated content and therefore advances the pool authority generation, while re-recording identical material moves nothing.

fence_readiness.description: The pool master's own answer to whether this host could be shut out, per method. Reported only by the master, only for the membership it owns, and never written into the durable record. Absent from a Core too old to report it, which a Controller shows as "not reported" and never as ready.

system_uuid_conflict_host_id.description: The member that already reported the hardware identity this host reports, when the master refused this host's report because of it. Without it the refusal is a dead end: an operator is told their host has no unique identity with nothing to act on. Cleared the moment the identity is accepted.

bmc.description: What this host's own Core found and did about its own management controller, reported to the master over the existing advertise peer route. It is an observation and a result, never a credential.

bmc_provisioning_disabled.description: The operator's own decision, recorded by the master, that this host must not configure its management controller for fencing. Clearing a fence device Nex Core provisioned sets it — one operator action with one meaning — and the host removes the account it created when it sees it. It is a decision, not an observation, so it lives with the fence profile in the replicated membership and a host cannot set or clear it by reporting about itself.

watchdog.description: This host's own watchdog capability, reported by the host and recorded by the master. A member too old to report one leaves it null, which is never counted.

watchdog_armed.description: That host's own report that it has armed its watchdog, recorded durably by the master. Null means the host never said, which is never a watchdog exclusion proof.

sanlock_host_id.description: Pool-master-assigned stable sanlock host ID. Zero or absent means this legacy member cannot participate in a storage lease.

sanlock_host_generation.description: Last native sanlock generation this host itself observed while its configured lease ID was live; not a proof by itself.

host_fencing_disabled.description: The pool's Host fencing setting, recorded the way it is decided: fencing is on for a pool that has never been told otherwise, so an absent field is on and a record written before the setting existed keeps the default. It is a decision, so it is durable, replicated and only ever written by the master.

fence_summary.description: The pool's fencing count, setting and prerequisite checklist, computed by the master over this membership when it reports it. Like the readiness on each member row it is a memory-only observation overlaid on the reported copy and never part of the durable record.

witness.description: The master's durable qdevice witness selection and CA pin. Runtime readiness is re-established from the native cluster after restart.

next_sanlock_host_id.description: Monotonic host-ID allocator watermark; prevents reuse after a member is ejected.

storage_lease.description: Reserved durable storage-lease configuration. The current product does not expose an accepted operator setup or automatic promotion workflow for it.

error.description: Sanitized refusal reason, emitted only with HTTP 409; CR, LF and NUL are replaced by a generic reason.

PoolPlacementReply.description: A read-only target-host observation. On 200, vm is an exact echo of the requested definition and accepted is true only when all native preflight checks passed. replay is present only when an identical existing target journal command was recognized; it cannot authorize a new master record. On 409, only error is emitted. The master must reject a missing, changed or false acknowledgement.

command.description: The supported subset of Command; operation_id must equal the enclosing operation_id and vm must be non-null.

PoolPlacementRequest.description: The exact managed vm-create or vm-update command that the master is about to admit; command.operation_id must equal operation_id.

name.description: replica-integrity: this host holds a verified signed replica. replica-supremacy: no reachable host holds a newer pool authority. accepted-ownership: every pool VM is recorded the same way by the host that owns it. old-master-exclusion: the old pool master has been fenced and its power-off observed by Core itself.

status.description: unknown blocks a promotion exactly as blocked does. It is a different word only so an operator can tell a refusal from an outage, and it is never presented as "fine". old-master-exclusion is normally unknown before the promotion runs, because Core fences and proves it during the promotion and never during a preflight.

hosts.description: The hosts this check is about.

vms.description: The pool VMs this check is about.

PoolPromotionCheck.description: One named check of the promotion proof, computed on the candidate from its own replica and its own live probes.

reachable.description: Whether the candidate reached this host over the pool network. An unreachable host is reported unreachable, never assumed stopped.

role.description: master or member, as that host answered.

authority_generation.description: The pool authority generation that host answered with.

replica_generation.description: The replica generation that host holds.

membership_generation.description: The membership generation that host holds.

blocks.description: This host's own answer to "does this host stop the promotion as things stand": an unreachable member that could itself have been promoted, or a reachable one that disagrees. A blocking host that can be fenced appears in the verdict's fence_host_ids; one that cannot is a refusal an operator must resolve another way.

fence_recorded.description: Whether a fence profile is recorded for this host at all.

fence_usable.description: Whether the candidate could turn that profile into a proof for this host: a profile kind this build can verify, plus a credential sealed to the candidate that it can open.

fence_unusable_reason.description: Core's own short sentence when it could not.

fence_kind.description: The recorded fence profile's kind, so a caller can show which method this promotion would shut this host out with. Empty when no profile is recorded.

fence_check_warning.description: Advisory only: what this candidate's own last non-destructive check of that fence device found, when it was failing or stale. The promotion's proof path is unchanged and still decides; this exists so an operator is not surprised by a fence device that was already known to be unreachable.

error.description: The probe's own bounded failure text.

PoolPromotionHost.description: One probed host of the replica's membership, as the promotion candidate found it, with that host's own contribution to the verdict: whether it blocks the promotion, and whether the candidate could exclude it by a fence if it does.

stage.description: The stage the candidate has durably reached: preflight, fence, activate, optional catalog-rebuild, repoint, done or aborted. A failed catalog import remains at catalog-rebuild with needs_attention until Core retries it.

status.description: needs_attention means durable and still running on Core, not an error.

error.description: The candidate's own last refusal or failure, bounded and sanitized.

verdict.description: The last verdict this host computed for the promotion.

cancellable.description: Core's own answer to "may this still be cancelled?". A promotion fences the old master, so it is never true; it is reported rather than inferred so a caller reads one field for every kind of transfer. It is always present: a caller reads one field for every kind of transfer and never has to tell "not cancellable" from "not reported".

observed_at.description: When this host wrote this report.

automatic.description: True only when Core initiated this promotion automatically through the supported two-host BMC path. Omitted for manual promotions and by older Core versions. This is reported metadata, not a fence proof. Automatic promotion requires Host fencing enabled; storage-lease and witness-based promotion paths are not implemented; qdevice registration and status do not produce fence proof.

PoolPromotionStatus.description: The promotion candidate's own report of the fence-verified promotion it is running. Reported as inventory.managed.promotion; the Controller stores no stage, no candidate and no verdict.

host_id.description: The host the pool authority records as this VM's owner.

state.description: confirmed by its reachable owner, fenced with its owner, or blocked. A blocked VM does not block the pool's promotion; it stays visible and unstartable until it is reconciled, and its definition is never deleted.

reason.description: Core's own sentence for a blocked VM.

PoolPromotionVM.description: One VM record of the replica, classified by the candidate against what the owning host itself reports.

candidate_host_id.description: The surviving member this verdict is about: the host that would become master.

old_master_host_id.description: The pool master this promotion would exclude.

operation_id.description: The promotion this verdict was computed for, when it belongs to one.

authority_generation.description: The generation the candidate would promote from.

can_promote.description: True only when the whole proof holds right now, fence included. In the normal ready state it is false, because the old master has not been fenced yet: that is an honest "not proved", not a refusal. A caller must not use it alone to decide whether to offer the promotion.

ready_to_fence.description: The state a caller offers the operator the promotion in: every check but the exclusion has passed, the exclusion is unknown only because no fence has been attempted, and the candidate holds a usable fence profile and an openable credential for every host in fence_host_ids. Confirming now proceeds to the fence rather than to a refusal.

fence_required.description: Whether this promotion needs a fence proof at all.

fence_recorded.description: Whether the old pool master has a fence profile recorded in the membership at all.

fence_usable.description: Whether this host could turn that profile into a proof: a profile kind this build can verify, plus a credential sealed to this host that it can open. Only virsh profiles can be recorded by this build, so a physical pool reports false.

fence_unusable_reason.description: Core's own short single-line sentence when it could not: "no fence profile is recorded for <host>", "this host holds no fence credential for <host>", or vmhost.PoolFenceUsable's own sentence such as "this host does not report a unique hardware identity, so a management controller cannot be confirmed to be its own".

fence_host_ids.description: Every host this promotion would power off, sorted: the old pool master, and every other host that blocks the promotion and can be excluded by a fence. It is what the operator confirms and what the promotion command carries back verbatim, so a host is never powered off without having been named to the operator first.

checks.description: Every named check, in Core's order.

hosts.description: Every host of the replica's membership, as the candidate probed it.

vms.description: Every pool VM of the replica, classified.

fence.description: The fence proof Core produced, when one exists. Always absent from a preflight: a preflight fences nothing.

blocking.description: Every blocking sentence, so a caller can show what must change without matching on check names. can_promote is exactly "this list is empty".

observed_at.description: When the candidate computed this verdict. A verdict is an observation with a lifetime, not a record: it is recomputed, never stored.

PoolPromotionVerdict.description: The promotion candidate Core's whole structured answer, computed on Core from its own signed replica and its own live probes of the pool network. A preflight returns it without changing anything, so an operator sees exactly what blocks before confirming a destructive fence. Nothing in it is computed, cached or stored by the Controller.

PoolReplicaAck.description: The member's answer to one push. Re-pushing the same generation with the same content returns the same acknowledgement; a refusal carries a bounded reason and a 409, never a silent drop.

host_id.description: The acknowledging member. Empty in a refusal that could not be attributed.

digest.description: Content digest of the stored replica: identical on every member of one generation, because the per-member address, the per-push wrap, the creation time, the signature and the generation are excluded from it.

verified.description: True only when the replica was verified against the pool CA, its sections recomputed, and the file durably written.

sanlock_host_generation.description: Native host generation in the configured authority lockspace after this member joined it; absent or zero means no sanlock preparation acknowledgement.

corosync_key_ready.description: True only after the addressed Corosync key was opened and durably stored; required by the master for a pool cluster replica.

error.description: Bounded refusal reason; control characters collapse the whole message to "pool authority replica refused".

PoolReplicaSection.description: One declared section of an authority replica and the SHA-256 of its canonical JSON. A member recomputes every digest and refuses a replica that declares a different set, so a section cannot be dropped, reordered or replaced.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of that section's canonical JSON.

PoolReplicaStatus.description: Observed replica state, reported in a member's inventory.managed.replica and returned by the peer GET. It is what a host holds and how fresh that observation is; the Controller mirrors it for display and stores none of it.

generation.description: 0 when this host holds no replica.

received_at.description: When this host stored it, from the host's own clock, so freshness survives a restart.

error.description: The last refusal this host recorded, kept alongside whatever it still holds; a later accepted push clears it. Includes "pool member refused backup authority page reuse" when a reusable blob cannot be safely staged.

kind.description: The structural form of reason, so no caller has to match on the sentence. unconfirmed is a master that has not re-proved its authority since it restarted; superseded is a host that found a higher authority elsewhere. Omitted by an older Core, in which case the sentence is the only signal.

reason.description: Why this host is refusing to act on pool authority.

conflicts.description: VMs this host still defines that the current pool master records as running elsewhere. A conflict is never resolved by guessing.

PoolRestrictedStatus.description: A Core-enforced refusal state on a host that cannot prove it holds the pool's current authority: while it is set the host writes no pool authority, mints no authority generation, starts no workload and autostarts nothing. Stop, power-off, console, local recovery access and reporting are untouched, and the libvirt hook refuses managed shared-VM starts by reading the host's own durable record, so the refusal holds with no Controller connected. It is reported by the authority probe, by inventory.managed.restricted and by GET /api/local/v1/pool.

identity.description: Core-canonical secret-free identity observed after member preparation.

locking.description: Member proved the shared non-blocking lock against the master for this generation.

PoolStorageLeaseConfig.description: Durable selection of the exact shared NFS repository used by the native sanlock storage-lease design. The feature is not available as an operator workflow and does not currently authorize automatic promotion.

PoolStorageLeaseExclusion.description: Native sanlock exclusion evidence shape. The corresponding two-host storage-lease proof path remains unavailable pending acceptance.

PoolStorageReservationRequest.description: Authenticated member-to-master peer request. The master binds the reservation to the mTLS member identity, not a client host field.

PoolStorageTransfer.description: One master repository record addressed to the calling member: storage.host_id is rewritten to the caller and member_access is cleared. credentials is present only for SMB repositories and carries the secret over peer mTLS; the member stores it only in its own Core credential state.

activated.description: The fact an abort needs: whether this host had already adopted the authority, decided once under its own lock, so an abort and an activation can never both succeed.

authority_generation.description: This host's authority generation after the step.

membership_generation.description: This host's membership generation after the step.

notice.description: Returned with an accepted activation: the new master's own signed re-point notice, so the outgoing master demotes itself on signed evidence rather than on its assumption that the activation worked.

PoolTransferReply.description: The addressed host's own answer to one transfer step.

operation_id.description: Idempotency key: the same request repeated after a lost reply returns the same answer and performs the step at most once.

action.description: activate hands the authority to the addressed host; abort records that it never activated and never will for this operation; repoint moves the addressed host onto the new master; leave tells an ejected host it has left.

PoolTransferRequest.description: One step of a transfer, addressed to one peer. abort carries no meaningful notice; every other action requires one whose operation_id matches.

operation_id.description: The Controller operation that started the transfer, or the identifier the transfer was recorded under.

action.description: promote or eject: Core's own name for what this transfer does. A fence-verified promotion of a surviving member is also promote, and is told apart by role: candidate. The Controller's requested action (master-change, eject, transfer-cancel) is reported separately in last_transfer.

role.description: This host's part in the transfer: source is the pool master that started it, target is the host taking the authority, ejected is the host leaving the pool, candidate is the surviving member running a fence-verified promotion.

target_host_id.description: The transfer's subject: the host becoming master, or the host being ejected.

stage.description: The stage this host has durably reached. For a master change: freeze, replicate, activate (the signed hand-off), repoint (every other host is told, in the new master's own signed words, who the master is now). For an eject: freeze, remove (the durable membership change, after which nothing stays frozen), repoint, leave. For a promotion: preflight, fence, activate, optional catalog-rebuild (after authority commit when repositories exist and the signed catalog is empty), repoint. A catalog import error leaves catalog-rebuild at needs_attention for retry before repoint, without reactivating or rolling back the committed master. done and aborted are terminal.

status.description: pending while the hosts are still running it; needs_attention means durable and still running, not an error.

error.description: This host's own last refusal or failure, bounded and sanitized.

authority_generation.description: The pool authority generation this transfer is pinned to.

frozen.description: True while this host is refusing pool authority writes for the transfer. Running guests are unaffected and stop is never refused.

cancellable.description: Core's own answer to "may this still be cancelled?", so no caller has to infer it from stage names. True only before the transfer's first irreversible durable step: a master change until the pool-CA-signed hand-off, an eject until the membership without that member is written, and never for a promotion, which fences. It is computed from the same predicate the cancel itself is gated on, so the reported flag and the accepted cancel cannot drift. It is always present: a caller reads one field for every kind of transfer and never has to tell "not cancellable" from "not reported".

handed_off.description: The outgoing master's own durable answer to "have I signed this pool's authority away?", reported rather than inferred from stage names or refusal sentences. Only the source records it, so a target or ejected host always reports false. It is always present, so an older Core that omits it is distinguishable from one that reports false.

observed_at.description: When this host wrote this report.

automatic.description: True only when Core initiated this promotion automatically through the supported two-host BMC path. Omitted for manual promotions and by older Core versions. This is reported metadata, not a fence proof. Automatic promotion requires Host fencing enabled; storage-lease and witness-based promotion paths are not implemented; qdevice registration and status do not produce fence proof.

PoolTransferStatus.description: One participant's own report of the master change or eject it is part of. Every participant reports its own; nothing merges them into a job, and a host that is not reporting says nothing rather than repeating its last stage.

aborted.description: Operation ID to journal proof that this exact next-revision vm-update failed while validating and was never applied, so the master can release a pending_update reservation whose reply it lost. An older member omits it, and the reservation stays blocked.

recoveries.description: VM ID to terminal evidence built by that VM owner's exact managed-journal record. In-progress, partial, unknown and failed-after-effects operations are omitted and remain reserved at the master.

deleted.description: VM IDs this member durably deleted: succeeded vm-delete tombstones from its own managed journal. Positive evidence of removal, which is what lets the master prune its pool-vms.json owner record for a VM; absence is never read as deletion.

start_outcomes.description: Exact failed owner-local start outcomes. A matching pending_start_operation_id, current authenticated owner, fresh shut-off observation and no pending definition or recovery transition are required to release a stopped reservation. Missing, uncertain and unrelated evidence leaves it reserved. Fresh running observation can independently confirm current execution without changing the task outcome.

detected_os.description: VM UUID to retained successful OS observation. Entries must belong to VMs in this inventory owned by the authenticated member in this pool; omitted entries preserve the master’s retained value. Only newer observations replace existing history. Older Core ignores this field. Upgrade Core throughout the pool before relying on history retention through master transfer or promotion.

PoolVMInventory.description: Complete, membership-generation-bound VM inventory of the reporting member. updates carries only exact successful local managed-journal evidence for a current revision; recoveries carries only exact terminal snapshot evidence from that VM's local managed journal; deleted carries this member's own delete tombstones.

host_id.description: The host that defines this VM, as that host itself reports it.

revision.description: The definition revision this host holds.

PoolVMOwnership.description: One host's own statement about one VM it defines, answered by the authority probe only when the caller asks for it. The execution epoch is deliberately absent: it is the master's number and a member could only repeat it back rather than confirm it. Consumed by the promotion proof of a later slice, which is not documented in this release.

snapshot.description: Required for completed snapshot-create evidence; absent on all other outcomes.

result_spec.description: Required only for completed revert; exact observed resulting VM specification must match the master-derived reservation hash. Absent on create and failed-before-effects.

PoolVMRecoveryEvidence.description: Owner-generated receipt for one exact terminal managed-journal record. Unknown, partial and failed-after-effects outcomes leave the reservation pending.

owner_operation_order.description: Nonzero durable owner command order for create, revert and delete; exact reservations and last settled receipts reject delayed older requests.

admission_refusal.description: A definitive no-effect snapshot-create refusal. It must settle only as failed-before-effects and cannot authorize native creation.

target_snapshot_id.description: Exact retained target ID; required only for revert.

target_snapshot_sha256.description: Canonical exact target descriptor hash; required only for revert.

result_spec_sha256.description: Master-derived expected restored VM specification hash; required only for revert.

PoolVMRecoveryReservation.description: Master-owned pending snapshot intent bound to exact owner/epoch, current VM/disk definition, native intent and operation order. Revert additionally binds the retained target descriptor and master-derived next specification; the master persists that pending result beside the reservation. Create admission_refusal is a definitive no-effect duplicate-name/full-catalog decision. Matching development Core versions are required.

epoch.description: Master execution generation. Start acknowledgement returns a nonzero epoch with the exact operation identity; completion of that start must echo both values. A stale epoch cannot settle a newer execution.

operation_id.description: Exact durable operation identity. Required for start admission; starting-to-running or starting-to-stopped completion must match the stored pending start identity and epoch. Also binds definition and recovery operations as described for their actions.

owner_operation_order.description: Required with snapshot-reserve; copied from the authenticated owner Core journal entry.

recovery_kind.description: Selects revert semantics on snapshot-reserve; absent/empty preserves existing create behavior.

captured_spec.description: Captured specification from the immutable owner journal, for revert only. Master verifies its canonical hashes/dependencies against the retained target before deriving the next VM revision.

placement_absent.description: Executing member attests that its local native journal, domain, target disk directories, NVRAM and TPM state are absent for the exact failed restore-as-new/test operation. Required true for release-restore-placement; uncertain observation refuses release.

placement_released.description: Master acknowledgement that the exact provisional VM owner row was durably removed, or was already absent on an exact retry. Required true before the member settles a definite pre-effect failure.

PoolVMRequest.description: Request and response share this shape: the master echoes the request after setting epoch and, per action, permit, spec_match, update_accepted, update_revision and placement_accepted. placement_accepted is true only after the master has received a fresh exact target-host preflight and durably recorded the create definition or update reservation. Older masters omit acknowledgement fields; clients must treat a missing acknowledgement as unsafe. delete-check requires the exact current VM definition and explicitly echoes vm_id, action, and spec_match=true only when the durable owner has no unresolved transition and no retained snapshot catalog entries; every VM delete must pass this check regardless of whether disk files will be retained or unlinked. Snapshot reservation echoes the exact durable reservation before native effects. Snapshot settlement is a bounded per-VM action: only an authenticated current owner can submit exact terminal evidence, and the owner clears its local reservation only after the master echoes the same evidence with snapshot_settled=true. Start admission durably records pending_start_operation_id with the incremented execution epoch. A member requires the exact echoed operation ID and nonzero epoch before starting; completion of that reservation requires both to match.
