Legacy starting records without the binding remain fenced. release-restore-placement binds an executing member's native absence attestation to the master's pending restore/test run, exact creator operation and untouched provisional owner record; a missing creator field from older Core cannot authorize release.

PoolVMSnapshot.description: Compact master-owned snapshot descriptor. Disk paths, XML and native artifacts remain in the owning Core journal.

PoolVMSnapshotCatalog.description: Compact durable catalog returned by the current pool master; contains no host paths or native XML.

PoolVMSnapshotDependencies.description: Sorted resource IDs referenced by the captured VM definition. Omitted on legacy descriptors when the historical dependencies are unknown.

PoolVMStartOutcome.description: Exact definitive failed start outcome from the executing Core journal, checked alongside fresh shut-off state. Start-after-create binds the base create operation ID, not the synthetic display outcome suffix; its journal must record failure before native dispatch.

armed.description: Whether this host is feeding a watchdog that will reset it if it stops. A host that is not armed says why in detail.

kind.description: The device class this host armed. emulated is a device a hypervisor presents to a host that is itself a virtual machine: it really does reset that machine, so Nex Core arms it, and every proof and row resting on one says so because a hypervisor reset is not evidence about hardware. A physical host never reports it.

device.description: The sysfs device name sbd was given.

timeout_seconds.description: How long after sbd stops feeding the device this host resets. A watchdog exclusion proof needs at least twice this.

fencing_generation.description: The pool membership generation this host armed at. A watchdog exclusion proof is refused unless this is the generation being promoted, so a host that armed under an earlier record of the pool cannot be shut out on the strength of it.

detail.description: Nex Core's own sentence for why this host is not armed, or why it could not be disarmed cleanly.

feeding.description: Whether this host's watchdog device is still being fed, which is not the same question as armed. armed is what the pool may rest a proof on and goes false the moment the pool decides this host should stop; the device itself is released only when that host's cluster next stops, which can be a pass or two later. Every other host needs the difference: a host that leaves the pool's cluster while a peer is still feeding can take that peer below quorum, and that peer resets with nothing wrong.

observed_at.description: When this finding last changed, in the manner of PoolHostBMC.observed_at — not when it was last confirmed. Nothing decides anything from it: staleness is fencing_generation, which is durable and replicated and therefore still readable by a candidate whose master has gone.

armed_at.description: The host's own clock when it started feeding this device, carried over unchanged while it goes on feeding the same one. Nothing compares it with another host's clock. It exists so that a host which stopped and started its watchdog — a reboot, a cluster restart — produces a record that differs from the one before it: an identical record is never written and never replicated, and a survivor would otherwise be unable to tell "armed since before it left" from "was armed once, and has been up unarmed since". A survivor refuses a watchdog proof against a target that rejoined its Corosync partition after the last armed record it holds.

PoolWatchdogArmed.description: A host's own report that it has armed its watchdog, kept in the pool master's durable membership and replicated. It is the first of the three conditions of a watchdog exclusion proof, and the host that has to read it is a promotion candidate whose master has gone, which is why it is durable rather than an observation.

kind.description: The device class the target armed, copied from its armed report. emulated means the target is itself a virtual machine, so this proof is evidence about a hypervisor and not about hardware.

timeout_seconds.description: The target's own watchdog timeout, as its armed report gave it.

armed_generation.description: The pool membership generation the target armed at, which must be the generation being promoted.

held_seconds.description: How long this host has continuously been in a quorate partition without the target, on a monotonic clock. Any flap — the target reappearing, quorum lost, or this agent restarting — restarts it from zero.

bound_seconds.description: How long that had to hold: at least twice the target's own timeout, and never less than a minute.

partition.description: The hosts Corosync reports in this host's partition at the moment of the proof, by the pool's own votequorum. It must not name the target and must be more than one host.

PoolWatchdogExclusion.description: The whole evidence of a watchdog exclusion, one field per condition of the rule, so a proof can be read back later and judged rather than believed. Nobody performed this fence: the target reset itself, and the proving host only established that it must have.

PoolWitnessCandidate.description: A qnetd candidate advertised by the Controller. Current Core uses only the controller candidate: same-site pool-master candidates have no CA or pin and are not usable.

ca_pem.description: PEM CA certificate; empty for an unusable pool-master candidate.

ca_sha256.description: Lowercase SHA-256 of the CA certificate DER; empty for an unusable pool-master candidate.

PoolWitnessRecord.description: The pool master's durable Controller qnetd selection and CA pin. Native readiness is re-established from Corosync and qdevice after restart; this record is replicated with pool authority.

PoolWitnessRegistration.description: Controller-signed qdevice credentials. address is empty for the Controller candidate; Core derives the qnetd address from its pinned Controller URL.

PoolWitnessRegistrationRequest.description: Core registration request. cluster_name is the deterministic name for pool_id; fencing_generation binds credentials to the current pool fencing configuration.

credential_ref.description: Core's own opaque reference for the material. It names a file in the host's state directory and is never projected to a client.

version.description: The master's counter for the material, so a member can tell a re-wrap of the same material from new material. It is mirrored in PoolMember.fence_credential_version, which is what makes rotated material advance the pool authority generation.

wrapped.description: The material sealed for this member alone, by the same primitive and with the same guarantees as the pool CA key, under its own context binding pool, member, generation, fenced host and reference.

PoolWrappedFenceCredential.description: One host's fence credential material carried to one member inside that member's replica. The host that actually fences during a promotion is a surviving member, and it cannot be given the material after the master it must fence is gone, so the material travels sealed rather than not at all. A member stores it sealed in its 0600 replica and opens it only while it performs a promotion; the Controller never sees it, and it never reaches SQLite, the audit trail, a response or a log. Every ready member can open the material addressed to it, which is the same trust model the sealed pool CA key already carries: admit only hosts you trust with powering off a profiled host.

PoolWrappedKey.description: The pool CA private key sealed for exactly one member of one generation: ECDH between a fresh ephemeral P-256 key and that member's certified peer public key, HKDF-SHA256 with a context binding pool ID, member host ID and generation, then AES-256-GCM with the same context as additional data. A member stores it sealed and never opens it while it is a member; nothing in this release unwraps it. All three fields are standard base64.

ephemeral_public_key.description: Base64 uncompressed P-256 point of the master's per-push ephemeral key.

nonce.description: Base64 12-byte AES-GCM nonce, fresh for every push.

ciphertext.description: Base64 AES-256-GCM ciphertext of the pool CA private key PEM.

PoolWrappedWitnessCredential.description: One host's native qdevice PKCS#12 credential, sealed to that host in its authority replica. It contains a shared qdevice key and is bound to the fencing generation.

RestoreAsNewRequest.description: Restores a recovery point as a new stopped VM from local copies.

host_id.description: Selected executing host; Core checks pool ownership.

RestoreReplaceRequest.description: Restores a recovery point over an existing VM identity with exclusive cutover.

host_id.description: Selected executing host; Core checks pool ownership.

filesystem_id.description: Diagnostic CIFS filesystem ID; it is not durable across reconnects.

marker_id.description: Core-created atomic durable share-root marker for new registrations. Core verifies it with the exact SMB source/options after reconnect. Absent only on preserved legacy records, which retain strict filesystem-ID failure behavior and are not auto-upgraded.

share.description: Ordinary share name: letters, numbers, internal spaces and ._$:()-; no leading/trailing whitespace or path/command/unit syntax.

directory.description: Validated existing relative subdirectory below the SMB share, including spaces; never an SMB path. Traversal, backslashes and control characters are rejected.

shared.description: Core-observed shared-storage capability, never by itself permission to place or start a VM. Provisioned ZFS is always false because each selected host has an independent local zpool.

StorageClusterConfig.description: Core-owned clustered-GFS2 projection. Controller relay input never grants a caller-owned device path, mount path, proof, or secret; Core derives/verifies those native details.

username.description: Management-controller account for redfish and ipmilan, with power control only. It is not a secret and is reported back; its password is the credential. Absent on virsh and scsi_pr profiles, and a BMC profile without one can never produce a proof.

tls_fingerprint.description: Core captures the certificate the controller presents when the profile is recorded, keeps its leaf SHA-256 here and holds every later connection to exactly it: a factory management controller is self-signed with no usable name, so this pin, not a chain, identifies the endpoint the password is sent to and the power-off is issued through. A changed certificate refuses the fence with its own sentence rather than as a network fault. Reported so an operator can compare it with the controller's own page; it is not a secret and a client never supplies one. Absent on ipmilan, which authenticates its RMCP+ session and presents no certificate, and on virsh and scsi_pr.

virsh_uri.description: For virsh, exactly qemu:///system or qemu+ssh://<ssh_login>@<endpoint>[:<ssh_port>]/system. The latter must match the pinned SSH fields; it rejects passwords, query strings, fragments and every other URI path. An omitted URI port is valid only when ssh_port is 22.

cipher.description: The RMCP+ cipher suite an ipmilan fence must use, as the controller's own LAN channel offers it. Core selects it itself — 17 where the controller offers it, otherwise 3, the suite every IPMI 2.0 controller must implement — either while provisioning the account in-band or while proving a profile an operator entered. Suite 0 asks for no authentication, no integrity and no confidentiality, so it is never selected and never accepted here. Absent means none was recorded and ipmitool's own default is used. A client never supplies it; a request that does is refused with 400.

provisioned_by_core.description: The account behind this profile is one Nex Core created on the host's own management controller in-band. It is how a host knows, after a reboot or a master change, that the account under the Nex name is its own to replace rather than somebody else's to leave alone, and it is why an operator-entered profile is never overwritten by automatic provisioning. Written only by the pool master when the host's own Core reports the account it created; a client never supplies it, and a request that does is refused with 400.

StorageClusterFence.description: Closed Core fence profile. credential_ref and ssh_host_key_ref are opaque names for root-only Core secrets, never secret bytes; arbitrary commands and arguments are not accepted. Before any power-off Core asks the management controller which machine it manages — the Redfish ComputerSystem.UUID, compared exactly, or IPMI Get System GUID, where either documented byte order counts — and compares it with the target host's own SMBIOS system UUID in the master's membership record. A mismatch, a host with no unique hardware identity and an unreadable controller each refuse the fence and power nothing off. Redirects are never followed, so the identity cannot be read from one machine while another is powered off. A Redfish fence is performed by Core itself over the pinned connection — identity GET, ComputerSystem.Reset ForceOff, then a separate PowerState read — rather than by fence_redfish, which cannot be bound to the recorded certificate. virsh is for a Nex Core running as a virtual machine in a disposable lab and remains unaccepted for native production use.

request_id.description: Optional stable ID of the actual destructive fence attempt. A Core verifies this binding before accepting a peer receipt.

method.description: How the exclusion was proved. Absent is a fence device Nex Core powered the host off through and independently observed off, which is every proof there was before watchdog fencing. watchdog is the host resetting itself, whose evidence is the record beside it. A clustered-storage fence only ever produces the absent one.

watchdog.description: The evidence of a watchdog exclusion, present only when method says so.

storage_lease.description: Native exclusion evidence shape; not currently enabled as an accepted promotion proof path.

StorageClusterFenceStatus.description: Core-recorded result of an actual fence/exclusion observation, bound to a request ID when destructive work was attempted and to an exact configuration generation and digest.

StorageClusterProjection.description: Private peer projection of one clustered-storage operation. auth_key is the pool corosync authkey; secrets are addressed only to the calling member. Must never cross the Controller boundary.

session_monitor_ready.description: Authenticated member attestation that the fixed local transport-monitor wrapper and CLI are installed and passed a successful live exact portal/IQN session probe. It is distinct from aggregate GFS2 or cluster health, and is projected to Controller only after storage-cluster-session-monitor-v1 is acknowledged.

StorageCredentials.description: Transient credential bytes only. Optional domain is the SMB workgroup or AD domain used with username/secret. The selected operation validates the applicable secret form; inventory, journals, results and diagnostics never carry these fields.

zfs_host_access.description: Current local access observations for each configured host of a Core-provisioned ZFS repository.

zfs_provisioned.description: True only for a repository created through Core ZFS provisioning.

zfs_scope.description: Requested ZFS scope (host or pool). Pool scope shares the Core repository identity across independent host-local zpools; it does not make storage shared.

StorageRegistration.description: Core-owned repository configuration and observation. A repository has one selected host in this release; shared is a capability observation, never placement permission. Source identity, access, capacity and health are Core observations; a missing or replaced mount blocks writes and never falls back to a mountpoint. For existing-dataset ZFS registration, source.zfs.mount_path remains the existing dataset mount and path is the Core-owned /var/lib/nex-storage/<repository-id> bind alias used by VM disks; detach removes only that alias and never ZFS properties. Core ZFS provisioning creates its own tagged pool and vms dataset, then uses the same alias. Credentials remain Core-local and inventory reports only presence. A fresh Controller adopts these records from Inventory.managed.storage.

TestRestoreRequest.description: Restores as a new VM marked for verification and later cleanup.

host_id.description: Selected executing host; Core checks pool ownership.

TestRestoreVerifyRequest.description: Records the operator verification result for a test restore.

firmware.description: uefi is the default and requires EFI firmware advertised by the host's libvirt domain capabilities; bios stays selectable.

machine.description: Empty selects Core's default machine type (q35).

media_boot_order.description: 0 keeps the CD drive out of the boot order; any other value joins the disks' contiguous 1..N numbering. Every VM has the drive, so the order is kept while it is empty and an ISO can be ejected from a running guest.

secure_boot.description: UEFI Secure Boot. Omitted means on with the Microsoft keys enrolled, which is exactly what libvirt already selected for every UEFI VM defined before this field existed, so a definition re-sent unchanged keeps the firmware its guest was installed with. off selects the plain OVMF build with no enrolled keys, for unsigned boot media or drivers. Requires uefi; on with bios is rejected. Core refuses the VM when the host's domain capabilities do not offer a matching firmware build, naming the setting rather than passing libvirt's firmware-selection error through. Changing it requires the VM to be shut off.

tpm.description: Emulated TPM. 2.0 adds a tpm-crb device backed by swtpm; omitted and none add no device, so a definition written before this field keeps exactly the devices it had. Windows 11 requires a TPM and refuses to install without one. Core refuses the VM when the host's domain capabilities do not advertise the emulator backend, rather than defining a device that cannot start. Changing it requires the VM to be shut off, and REMOVING a TPM is refused outright at any time: anything the guest sealed to it, including a Windows BitLocker key, would be lost, and libvirt cleans TPM state by iterating the devices the persistent definition still carries, so a redefine without it would orphan that state.

VMBoot.description: Firmware, Secure Boot, TPM, machine type and the install media's place in the boot order. Boot order is per device (libvirt forbids mixing per-device boot with an os/boot device list), so at least one disk or the install media must carry a non-zero order.

count.description: vCPUs presented to the guest. Both sides require at least 1; Controller caps the request at 64 and refuses more than the host reports.

sockets.description: Sockets, or 0 with cores and threads for the default topology.

cores.description: Cores per socket, or 0 for the default topology.

threads.description: Threads per core, or 0 for the default topology.

model.description: Host modes follow the current host; named models come from native host capabilities. New wizard drafts choose the current pool CPU baseline when available, storing its exact model/features. Explicit feature-bearing definitions are compared against the actual VM machine and runtime. Baseline compatibility covers current members only, not future hosts or live migration. CPU choices are independent of guest OS.

features.description: Optional fixed native CPU feature list. Omitted or empty retains model-only behavior. Nonempty requires a named model (not host modes or max) and vm-cpu-baseline-v1. Duplicate feature names are rejected.

VMCPU.description: vCPU count, optional topology and CPU model. Sockets, cores and threads all 0 select the default topology of one socket, count cores and one thread; otherwise each must be at least 1 and sockets × cores × threads must equal count. JSON Schema cannot express that product, so Controller and Core both enforce it in protocol.ValidateVMSpec.

id.description: Controller-assigned stable UUID; identity is preserved across Controller replacement and later migration.

name.description: Nonblank VM name, at most 200 UTF-8 bytes (the byte limit is additionally enforced by Controller and Core). Spaces, case, dots, punctuation and Unicode are preserved exactly. Slashes, control characters and XML-invalid U+FFFE/U+FFFF are rejected. Core checks uniqueness on the host, journals the name and reports it for Controller adoption; failed or uncertain creations retain their reservation. Upgrade Controller and Core together to use the expanded naming syntax.

description.description: Free-text operator note, at most 4096 characters.

guest_os.description: Guest OS hint recorded for display and guest-tools advice; empty leaves it unset. It installs nothing and does not change the VM devices: disk bus and NIC model are chosen per device.

disks.description: One to eight disks; names unique within the VM.

media_id.description: Install ISO (Media.id), empty for none. The ISO must be imported and verified on the placement host; it may live on any storage that host can read and does not need to share a repository with the VM's disks. Every VM has the CD drive, so a non-zero boot.media_boot_order does not require media_id: an emptied drive keeps its place in the boot order.

drivers_media_id.description: ISO in the VM's second CD drive, for a driver disc an installer needs alongside its install media - a Windows guest installing to a VirtIO disk needs the virtio-win ISO here. Empty leaves that drive empty; the drive itself always exists on a host reporting vm-media-drivers-drive-v1. Must differ from media_id.

start_after_create.description: Honoured by the host inside the creation, after the definition is verified, so the creation itself has succeeded whether or not the flag is set: Core starts the guest exactly once and records the outcome in the journal entry's start field. A failed automatic start leaves the VM defined and stopped as a normal managed VM (power, console and media work; a replacement Controller adopts it) and is reported by the host as its own outcome with ID <operation-id>:start, kind vm-power, status failed and error 'VM created but not started: <reason>', which Controller records in Task history. A creation interrupted at the start step reconciles by observing libvirt: running means started, otherwise that outcome reads 'interrupted before the automatic start completed'. A failed or uncertain creation never boots. Controller issues no follow-on power request. Must be false in an edit.

autostart.description: libvirt autostart, set while the stopped guest is defined so the host starts this VM on boot. It is not a start.

tags.description: Operator labels kept with the VM definition: each 1 to 32 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens, at most 16. Controller sorts and de-duplicates them before validation; an invalid tag is 400 naming it (tag "<tag>" must be 1 to 32 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens), more than 16 distinct tags is 400 (a VM allows at most 16 tags). Tags are part of the complete definition, so an edit that omits them clears them. Nonempty tags need vm-tags-v1 on both the VM's host and its pool master, because an older Core would drop them: 409 "the VM's host or its pool master does not support VM tags; upgrade Nex Core" on updateVM and "the selected host or its pool master does not support VM tags; upgrade Nex Core" on createVM, after the replay check. Core journals them with the definition, the pool master keeps them in its pool VM record, and a fresh Controller adopts them from the host's reported definition. Omitted when empty and from older Core. They change no guest device and apply to a running VM. Introduced in development product 0.4.8.

revision.description: Definition revision: 0 at creation, current + 1 for each edit. Core refuses any other value, so a stale edit after Controller replacement fails instead of applying an old definition. Reported back in Inventory.managed.vms with the current definition.

VMCreateSpec.description: The complete VM specification: Controller-assigned UUID and pool membership with separate host assignment, identity, CPU, memory, every disk and network interface, boot and install media, and the two lifecycle switches. Creation defines a stopped VM and never boots it. Dependencies must have succeeded on this host and pool. Both sides validate the shared bounds through protocol.ValidateVMSpec; Controller owns identity, reference existence, pool-wide MAC uniqueness and capacity.

storage_id.description: Registered storage that has succeeded on this VM's host and pool. Core resolves it by resource ID, not by pool/host ID, so it survives Controller replacement.

name.description: Operator-facing disk name, unique within the VM. Letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore, starting with a letter or digit; it is not a path.

bus.description: virtio needs guest drivers (built into Linux, virtio-win on Windows); sata and scsi work without them.

thin.description: true creates a sparse qcow2 that grows on use; false preallocates the full size.

boot_order.description: 0 keeps the disk out of the boot order. Non-zero values are unique across every disk and boot.media_boot_order and number the boot devices from 1 with no gaps.

VMDisk.description: One virtual disk, created inside the VM's own exclusive directory on its storage target. Disks are never shared or reused: Core checks exclusive ownership for every disk and free space per storage target, summing the disks that land on the same target.

mode.description: dedicated preallocates and locks the ceiling in host RAM while running: memory and currentMemory at size_mib, no balloon, and memoryBacking with immediate allocation, locked and nosharepages. Stopped VMs release physical RAM but retain their Nex capacity commitment. QEMU overhead is locked too. Requires updated Core; existing VMs need full shutdown, a successful stopped vm-update save and start. Legacy dedicated live edits fail before device effects with a stop-and-save instruction. Upgrade, autostart or guest reboot alone does not rewrite old definitions. maximum caps without reserving: the same ceiling plus a virtio balloon with free page reporting, so the guest returns pages it frees. Reclaim requires the balloon driver running in the guest (built into Linux; virtio-win guest tools on Windows); without it the guest drifts to the ceiling and holds it. There is no pressure-driven reclaim daemon.

size_mib.description: Memory ceiling in MiB. Both sides require at least 512; Controller caps the request at 262144.

VMMemory.description: Memory ceiling and how the host treats it. size_mib is the ceiling in both modes and host capacity preflight uses that ceiling in both modes: a VM that cannot reach its ceiling is refused. dedicated additionally counts against committed capacity; maximum reserves nothing and is allowed to oversubscribe.

network_id.description: Registered network that has succeeded on this VM's host and pool, resolved by resource ID.

model.description: Which network card the guest sees. virtio is paravirtualised: fastest and lowest host CPU, but the guest needs a driver (built into Linux, virtio-win on Windows). e1000 and e1000e emulate Intel gigabit cards nearly every OS already drives, for guests and installers that cannot see a virtio adapter, at higher host CPU. rtl8139 emulates a 100 Mbit card for guests too old for a gigabit driver; the limit is the emulated hardware. vmxnet3 is VMware's paravirtualised adapter, for guests already carrying VMware drivers.

mac.description: Empty derives a stable MAC from the VM ID and the interface index (protocol.DerivedMAC: the 52:54:00 locally administered prefix, two octets of sha256(id) and the index), which never collides across a VM's at most 8 interfaces. A manual address must be six octets in canonical lower-case colon form and unicast; the pattern encodes the cleared multicast bit as an even second hex digit. All-zero addresses are refused, addresses are unique within the VM, and Controller additionally enforces uniqueness across the pool by plain string comparison. The VM list reports the effective address, and an edit freezes every automatic address into the definition (drawn from the VM's derived range above the highest index the VM uses, or the lowest free index when none above is free), so interfaces keep their identity across later edits.

mtu.description: Interface MTU, or 0 for the network's own. Accepted only when model is virtio: QEMU communicates an MTU to the guest through virtio's host_mtu feature and libvirt sizes the host tap to match, while the emulated models have no equivalent and would leave the guest on its own default. A value on any other model is refused rather than silently applied to the host side only. The floor is the IPv6 minimum MTU and the ceiling the largest jumbo frame common NICs accept; every device along the path must agree or traffic is dropped without an error.

VMNIC.description: One virtual network interface on a registered pool network. A VM may have none and at most 8.

snapshot_id.description: Retained target ID for revert, distinct from the command operation ID; absent on create.

target.description: Exact master catalog descriptor resolved internally by Core for revert; absent on create and never supplied through the operator endpoint.

mode.description: Create capture mode. Omitted or stopped requires a shut-off guest. crash and quiesced require a running guest; quiesced also requires a responding guest agent. UEFI running capture is refused in this development slice.

VMSnapshotRequest.description: Core snapshot command payload. Create requires nonempty name and optional description and mode (omitted/stopped, crash, or quiesced), with no target. Revert requires snapshot_id and the exact internally resolved target descriptor, with empty name and description.

VMUpdateEvidence.description: Untagged Go struct: JSON members use Go field names.

ZFSHostAccess.description: Current per-host observation for a Core-provisioned local ZFS repository. The GUIDs, path, capacity and read/write flags apply only to host_id; a missing or errored observation grants no placement permission.

parent.description: replacing or spare when this leaf sits under an in-flight replacement or activated-spare vdev; omitted for an ordinary data leaf.

ZFSPoolDevice.description: One leaf of the pool's vdev tree, named as the pool was created: the /dev/disk/by-id path for a Core-provisioned repository. parent marks an in-flight replacing or spare vdev.

ZFSPoolScan.description: A running or completed scrub or resilver. ZFS formats its own sizes and timestamps, so they are reported as the strings it produced.

ZFSPoolStatus.description: Core's transient `zpool status` observation of one imported pool. Nothing durable is derived from it: the Controller passes it through and a fresh Controller sees it again on the next report.

spares.description: Hot spares. They are erased like the data disks, added as spare vdevs and the pool is created with autoreplace=on, so ZFS resilvers onto one by itself when a data disk fails. They satisfy no part of the layout rule.

ZFSProvisionHostResult.description: Durable outcome for one selected host. pool_guid and dataset_guid identify that host's independent native zpool and dataset after a successful provision; this outcome alone is not a current access observation.

ZFSReplaceRequest.description: Replace one failed leaf device of a provisioned ZFS repository's pool on one host. old_device names the leaf exactly as the pool observation reports it, and device is one candidate from POST /api/v1/storage/discover with kind zfs-device, carrying the same identity, fingerprint and typed erase confirmation rules the ZFS wizard uses. Core revalidates both against a fresh observation of the pool and the disk before it touches anything.

operation_id.description: Core operation identity. The executing host journals its replacement under it, so a redelivered command replays the recorded outcome instead of acting again.

host_id.description: The configured host whose pool holds the failed disk. It may be the pool master or a ready current member.

old_device.description: The failed leaf's /dev/disk/by-id path, as the repository's pool observation reports it.

mount_path.description: Original existing ZFS dataset mount path. It rejects Unicode whitespace/control characters, percent and backslash because Core uses it as a systemd What value.

state.description: Operating means the pool master verified the selected qdevice's identity, pinned CA, TLS connection and cast vote. It does not imply an armed watchdog or an automatic fence proof.

detail.description: Core's current native observation or reason the witness is still forming.

os.description: Last successful guest-get-osinfo display name; 1–4096 UTF-8 bytes.

os_id.description: Optional guest-reported OS identifier; at most 200 UTF-8 bytes.

observed_at.description: Nonzero Core timestamp of the successful guest-agent OS observation, not the inventory/report time.

DetectedOS.description: Durable historical OS identity retained by Core. It does not establish current guest-agent availability or guest health.

PoolUpdateStep.description: One idempotent rollout step (peer step route). step_id is deterministic per (rollout, host, stage): a repeat is the same step and is answered from the host's current state, never run twice. Actions: check (verify the release is offered), stage (stage only; never arms the next boot), drain (gracefully shut down exactly vm_ids), activate (arm and reboot; the engine keeps its refuse policy), confirm, undrain (start exactly vm_ids through master start admission) and rollback.

PoolUpdateStepResult.description: done false with no code means still running: ask again with the same step_id. code is the host engine's stable refusal code.

PoolUpdateHostStatus.description: One host's own read-only observation of its image engine and guests (peer status route).

PoolUpdateRollout.description: The pool master's durable rollout record (pool-update.json beside pool-peer.json), replicated as the optional authority-replica section update_rollout (declared only while a record exists). A promoted master finds an active rollout paused with pause.code master_changed and an operator decides resume or abort. Hosts' own progress is in each host's state.json. Reported in Inventory.managed.update_rollout by the master only, withheld until the Controller acknowledges image-update-v1. id is the request_id that started it; finalized_sequence is set only once every host committed the release.

PoolUpdateHost.description: The master's record of one host's progress in a rollout. stage is the next unfinished step: pending, staged, maintenance, teardown, drain, activate, boot, confirm, release, restart, soak, done or rolled_back. stopped_by_update lists the guests this rollout shut down on the host; it is written before the shutdown is requested, so a crash never loses which guests owe a restart.

PoolUpdatePause.description: Why a rollout is paused. code is one of operator_paused, master_changed, needs_attention, running_vms, step_timeout, rolled_back, unconfirmed, quorum_margin, host_busy, ha_enabled, membership_changed.

PoolUpdateTarget.description: What a host verified about the release it was asked to install.

PoolUpdateRequest.description: Request of the update-rollout and update-control pool commands. sequence and running_vms (refuse waits for every guest to stop then pauses naming them; shutdown gracefully shuts the host's guests down, records stopped_by_update and restarts them on the same host through master start admission; evacuate is refused evacuation_unavailable) start a rollout; dry_run runs only the preflight; rollout_id, control (pause, resume, abort, rollback_host) and host_id address an existing one.

BackupS3Source.description: S3-compatible HTTPS endpoint, bucket, optional prefix and signing region for a backup destination.

endpoint.description: HTTPS endpoint with verified TLS identity.

BackupSFTPSource.description: SFTP host, root path and pinned SSH host-key fingerprint for a backup destination.

BackupRemoteIdentity.description: Observed remote destination fingerprint used for S3 and SFTP identity checks.

BackupRepositoryHealthTransition.description: Historical repository health transition; not a fresh access result.

PeerBackupCredentialRequest.description: Private credential delivery from current pool master to a ready member. Never persisted by Controller or returned in inventory.

recipient_host_id.description: Authenticated member for whom this private credential projection was prepared.

PeerSMBCapabilityRequest.description: Portable Core-owned SMB3 backup repository and exact master-observed share identity for member preflight.

PeerSMBCapabilityResponse.description: Member-observed identity proof for this exact repository and private credential receipt.

PeerS3CapabilityResponse.description: Member-observed S3 identity proof for this exact repository and private credential receipt.

PeerSFTPCapabilityResponse.description: Member-observed SFTP identity proof for this exact repository and private credential receipt.

BackupOrphanCleanup.description: The pool master's durable record of one orphaned-backup cleanup: the planned points and each one's outcome.

OrphanCleanupRequest.description: Deletes the recovery points of the chosen VMs, which are not in the pool's VM inventory, from a repository's destination and catalog.

vm_ids.description: VMs chosen explicitly; there is no wildcard.

include_protected.description: Also delete protected points; otherwise they are skipped.

confirmation.description: 'delete N recovery points', or 'delete N recovery points including P protected' with include_protected.

recovery_points.description: Recovery points of the chosen VMs the operator was shown.

protected_points.description: How many of them are protected.
